newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hamas fugitive turns himself in, PLO says.
newsitem.headline: Hamas fugitive turns himself in, PLO says.

text.p: A fugitive Hamas guerrilla turned himself in to Palestinian forces in Hebron on Monday, four days after breaking out of jail, PLO security officials said.
They said the guerrilla, Ibrahim Ghneimat, had been a senior member of a Hamas Islamic guerrilla cell that carried out several attacks against Israelis.
He escaped from a PLO prison in Hebron on Thursday but "returned to the jail by himself" in the West Bank town early on Monday, the sources said
Ghneimat was among several Hamas guerrillas rounded up by Israel and Yasser Arafat's Palestinian Authority in April, following a March bombing in Tel Aviv in which three Israeli women were killed.
The cell also kidnapped and killed an Israeli soldier.
PLO security forces had mounted an intensive search for Ghneimat since his Thursday escape, Hebron residents said.
Israeli military authorities had cast doubt on the escape report, saying it was likely PLO jailers had released Ghneimat.

The West Bank town, 80 percent of which is controlled by the Palestinian Authority under a peace deal with Israel, has been wracked by violence since an Israeli woman sparked Arab Moslem rage 10 days ago by posting placards portraying the Prophet Mohammad as a pig.
